newsitem.title: FINLAND: CHALLENGES FOR FINLAND IN EUROPEAN BUSINESS STUDY.
newsitem.headline: CHALLENGES FOR FINLAND IN EUROPEAN BUSINESS STUDY.

text.p: Tackling high taxes, government spending and labour rigidity and integrating Eastern Europe into the EU are the main challenges facing Finnish business, said a new European study published on Wednesday.

"These are the three issues (of main importance) in Finland: High tax level and government spending, lack of labour flexibility, and integration of Eastern Europe into the European Union," Osvald Bjelland, managing director of the Performance Group, told a news conference.
The Performance Group is an Oslo and London-based consulting group.
Participants in the EuroStudy, which surveyed 83 top European business leaders including six from Finland, identified five steps that Europe would need to take to become more competitive.
* Reduce the barriers to growth that have created record-high levels of structural unemployment.
* Invest in the kind of coordinated transportation and telecommunications infrastructure that Europe will need to be competitive in the 21st century.
* Stress educational reform that links learning to work.
* Broaden the EU to allow participation by the new, democratic countries of Eastern Europe.
"Europe is already one of the biggest markets in the world, and it is possible to turn it into one of the fastest-growing if we do the five things in the report," Bjelland said.

The Finnish industrialists who participated in the survey were Ahlstrom CEO Krister Ahlstrom, Metra CEO Georg Ehrnrooth, Neste CEO Jaakko Ihamuotila, Kesko deputy chief executive Timo Karake and Outokumpu CEO Jyrki Juusela.
The study called for restoration of European competitiveness through growth of new businesses.

"We need a growth agenda," Georg Ehrnrooth told the news conference. "We (in Europe) have lost market share on the world market and on our domestic markets. We are less competitive than we used to be," he said.

"Europe is today, in many respects, too expensive, too inflexible and with high labour costs not only in relation to salaries but also to total costs and payment for perks," Ehrnrooth was quoted as saying in the report.
"The labour market is not functioning as a market in Europe because of very strong labour unions and because of the labour laws," Neste CEO Jaakko Ihamuotila said in the report.
